summary: Make the 38-entry integration catalog fail closed against one generated runtime-support contract and extend the audited built-in composition from six to eleven executable product connectors without broadening the worker beyond the product entity.

impacts.evidence: Account, capability, runtime-config and health operations retain the existing organization/workspace repository scope; the build-time support contract contains no tenant data.
The new contract contains connector IDs, capability names and non-secret configuration examples only; no persisted or event field and no retention policy changes.
Wire shapes and paths are unchanged. Requests for manifest-only connectors or capabilities now fail closed with HTTP 422 instead of creating non-executable runtime state.
No event envelope, schema, topic, producer payload or consumer compatibility change.
Connector SDK v1 and canonical manifests are unchanged. Runtime readiness is a separate host-owned contract and cannot grant a provider new SDK capability.
Runtime readiness is generated build metadata; no schema or existing tenant row changes.

Unsupported accounts, capability selections and entity directions are denied before remote execution. Five added connectors remain inside the policy-pinned ADR-0090 composition and host-mediated HTTPS boundary.
Only exact runtime-supported capabilities can be enabled; existing capability risk and approval metadata remain authoritative for the admitted operations.
Existing connector account and configuration audit capture is retained; rejected requests create no external effect or misleading success record.
Policy admission now checks the exact connector/entity/direction before existing durable cursor, receipt and idempotency mechanisms can dispatch it.
New product adapters use the existing HTTPS-only, DNS-pinned, public-address-only, redirect-disabled host transport; no outbound webhook behavior changes.
Ready connector health checks exercise the concrete adapter/configuration path, while planned connectors return a bounded unavailable response rather than a false healthy state.
Rollback is a binary rollback with no data migration. Existing accounts remain recoverable and can be disabled; unsupported runtime authority is restored only by an explicit contract revision.
Generation checks exact manifest parity and capability subsets; Go tests cover support directionality and registry resolution, and frontend tests/build cover the three availability stages.
